title: Rabbi Abba bar Mimi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Shir HaShirim Rabbah, chapter 1, on Naavu [compare 1:10:2]](https://www.sefaria.org/Shir_HaShirim_Rabbah.1.10.2), mentions him favorably when describing scholars engaging with one another over halakhah, such as Rabbi Abba bar Mimi and his colleagues. Hyman says they are not found elsewhere. R' Yerucham Leiner, in Seder HaDorot HaShalem, suggests that [Rosh Hashanah 35a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.35a.1), “When R' Abba came up from the sea,” should instead read bar Mimi.

notes.text: The supplied מייללין remains lexically uncertain; the rendering gives the broad activity without deciding whether it means disputing, sharpening or another form of discussion. Rashi explains Rosh Hashanah35a מימי as returning from a sea voyage; Leiner instead proposes the patronym bar Mimi. The proposed identification remains open.

[Rashi’s gloss](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Rosh_Hashanah.35a.1.1) understands מימי as a return from a sea voyage. Hyman reports Leiner’s suggestion that the text originally had the patronymic bar Mimi.

Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:10:2 names Rabbi Abba bar Mimi and his colleagues as examples of scholars exploring halakhah together. Rosh Hashanah 35a has מימי, which Rashi explains as Rabbi Abba’s return from a voyage at sea. Hyman attributes the proposed wording bar Mimi to Leiner. Both that suggestion and the exact sense of the midrash’s verb remain open.
